status.note: Chosen for modality. Tooltip established that layering has no home; a dialog adds focus containment, background inertness and a dismissal key, and none of those are the same problem. Sourced from the W3C ARIA APG modal dialog pattern, which is normative and complete.

intent.purpose: Interrupts what a person was doing to ask for something that cannot wait, and refuses to let them continue until they answer or leave.
behaviour: Shows over the page with everything behind it made inert: not merely covered, but unreachable by pointer, by Tab and by a screen reader's virtual cursor.
Moves focus inside when it opens, onto the first meaningful control rather than the close button, and holds focus inside for as long as it is open.
Returns focus, on close, to whatever had it before — otherwise a keyboard user is dropped at the top of the document.
Closes on Escape from anywhere inside it.
Names itself from its own title, so it is announced as the thing it is asking about rather than as an unnamed dialog.
notFor: Anything that can be said in place. A dialog stops everything; a message that could have been a line of text under a field should be.
Non-modal side content. A panel that lets you keep working is a drawer or a popover, and modality is the whole difference.
Nesting. A dialog opened from a dialog leaves a person two escapes from where they were, and no design here covers where focus returns.
Anything long enough to scroll on a phone. A full-screen sheet is a different pattern with different dismissal rules.

open.description: The dialog is showing and holding focus.
open.visual: The scrim covers the page and the panel appears above it.

size.description: How wide the panel is. A contiguous subset of the canon's ladder.

a11y.keyboard: Escape closes from anywhere inside. Tab and Shift+Tab cycle within the dialog and never leave it while it is open.
notes: Focus containment is the whole pattern, and NONE of it is expressible here. A dialog that can be tabbed out of is not modal, and a screen-reader user who reaches the page behind it is being lied to about what is interactive.

The background must be inert, not merely covered. A scrim that only paints over the page still leaves every control behind it focusable and readable, which is the most common way this pattern is got wrong.
Focus must return to the element that opened the dialog. Nothing here records what that was, and dropping focus to the document start is disorienting in a way sighted users never see.
The dialog is named by its title. A dialog with no title is announced as an unnamed dialog, and nothing here detects that.
Escape must close it. That is a keyboard behaviour that is not activation, and there is no way to declare one.

title.description: What the dialog is asking about. Required: it is the dialog's accessible name.

actions.description: The buttons that resolve it. Fills the `actions` part.

root.description: The layer holding the scrim and the panel. Covers the viewport while open.

panel.description: The dialog itself. Named by its title, and the region focus is held inside.

title.description: The heading. Supplies the dialog's accessible name.

actions.description: The row of buttons that resolve it.
